newsitem.title: UK: IFC emerging market index extends week's gains.
newsitem.headline: IFC emerging market index extends week's gains.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation's composite index of emerging market equities, denominated in dollars IFC/IPRD, extended this week's gains, rising 0.7 percent to 319.27 at the start of play on Thursday.
The level represents a new 1997 high.
Latin America rose 0.5 percent day-on-day to 597.14, Asia was up 0.3 percent at 262.57, and Europe, Middle East and Africa were up 1.8 percent at 152.61.
The IFC composite index began 1997 at 294.37, after making gains of 7.0 percent over the course of 1996.
ING Barings' Global Emerging Market Index (BEMI), also denominated in dollars BFFO, was up 0.56 percent day-on-day at 173.35 at 1015 GMT.
It began 1997 at 159.57 after rising 8.9 percent over the course of 1996. It touched a high of 171.22 after the end of trading on January 20.
Morgan Stanley's dollar-denominated Emerging Markets Free index .CEMF=USD was up 0.53 percent at 514.413, calculated after the close of trade on Wednesday.
It began 1997 at 476.315 after making gains of 3.9 percent over 1996. Its 1997 high of 508.674 was also reached on January 20.

All indices are capitalisation-weighted and are calculated daily. The IFC index measures returns on equities, liquid and accessible to foreign investors, from 30 emerging market countries after adding Russia, Slovakia, Egypt and Morocco on February 3. It is updated at 2300 GMT.
The BEMI index measures equity returns without dividends from some 21 emerging market countries, with the latest changes reported by 0900 GMT.
The MSCI Free measures equity returns without dividends from 26 emerging market nations. Changes are reported by 1300 GMT.
